name: Zone 1 · Daily - Raised beds below house
notes:
What it is: the main vegetable beds, about 150 m² on the slope below (north-east of) the house – raised beds for bulk vegetables, fruiting crops and roots, with the morning sun.
Water: clean water only (roof or creek tank by drip, area A) – these are food crops eaten fresh, so no laundry or treated water here. Budget about 3,750 L/week in the dry spring (2,500 L per 100 m²); add a small tank or header feed if the 20,000 L tank is far.
Layout: 4–6 raised beds 1.2 m wide across the slope (log, sleeper or corrugated sides), 0.6 m mulched paths; rotate crop families bed by bed each season.
Mix Aug–Nov (now): cherry tomato, capsicum, chilli, eggplant, basil (get them in before the wet); cucumber and watermelon by Nov; snake beans and cowpea.
Mix Dec–Feb (wet): sweet potato, snake beans, amaranth, Ceylon spinach – hardy crops that cope with heavy rain; leave one bed under green manure.
Mix Mar–Aug (main season): carrot, beetroot, radish, peas and snow peas, garlic, kale, silverbeet, broccoli, bok choy.
Bed ends and edges: pigeon pea for windbreak and chop-and-drop, marigold and basil for pests, a comfrey patch for mulch.
Tips: compost and mulch thickly (sandy soil); keep taro, kang kong and cape gooseberry in their own contained bed if grown at all.
From the water-source plan (18 Oct) – adjust on site.
